notes: Curated starter categories for planning context. These mappings are product assumptions for filtering CBP facts; they are not legal, financial, zoning, or market advice.
requiredBeforePlanningEndpoint: Validate category labels and assumptions with product review.
Confirm CBP NAICS coverage and suppression behavior for each mapped code family.
Decide how aggregate NAICS codes should be handled before ranking or scoring.
Keep confidence and limitations visible in any planning response.

categories.description: Food service establishment such as a restaurant, cafe, limited-service eatery, or drinking place.
assumptions: Needs customer access, food-service permitting, utilities, and location-specific zoning review.
CBP activity can show related establishment presence but not current demand or site viability.
limitations: Does not separate cuisine, service model, capacity, or alcohol licensing.
Does not estimate foot traffic, revenue, rent, or permit approval likelihood.

categories.description: Neighborhood-scale food, grocery, or convenience retail establishment.
assumptions: Needs customer access, supply logistics, refrigeration/utilities, and local retail compatibility review.
ACS and accessibility data are needed before drawing demand or access conclusions.
limitations: Does not distinguish small neighborhood groceries from larger supermarkets.
Does not account for inventory model, delivery radius, or food-access need.

categories.description: Ambulatory health, medical office, clinic, or outpatient service establishment.
assumptions: Needs licensing, accessibility, utilities, and professional workforce review.
Education institution proximity is only a weak context signal until program and workforce data are added.
limitations: Does not model provider specialty, payer mix, regulation, or certificate requirements.
Does not estimate community health need or provider shortage.

categories.description: Software, technical consulting, or lower-impact office-based service activity.
assumptions: Often has lower land-use complexity than food, lodging, or clinical uses.
Needs broadband, workforce, and office suitability context before strong planning signals.
limitations: Does not distinguish remote-first, client-facing, or back-office operating models.
Does not measure broadband quality, labor availability, or customer demand.

assumptions: Needs tourism context, zoning, hazard, infrastructure, and permit review.
CBP establishment presence is not a substitute for lodging demand or occupancy data.
limitations: Does not include short-term rental platform activity.
Does not evaluate tourism flows, seasonality, property availability, or hazard exposure.

categories.description: Construction contractor or trade service business.

mappedNaics.title: Electrical contractors and other wiring installation contractors

assumptions: Related activity may be better understood once permit trends are added.
Workforce and storage/yard needs vary widely by trade.
limitations: Does not cover every construction trade or contractor scale.
Does not infer project demand, bonding capacity, or permitting workload.

categories.description: Office-based professional, technical, consulting, accounting, legal, or advisory service.

mappedNaics.title: Administrative management and general management consulting services
All other professional, scientific, and technical services

assumptions: Usually office-oriented, but client access, workforce, and business density still matter.
Category is intentionally broad and should be narrowed for specialized planning.
limitations: Combines many professional services with different demand drivers.
Does not estimate client base, pricing, or licensing needs.

categories.description: Instructional, tutoring, vocational, or training-service establishment.
assumptions: Needs population, workforce, education ecosystem, and zoning/use context.
Existing institution presence may indicate ecosystem context but can also indicate competition.
limitations: Does not distinguish accredited institutions from informal training services.
Does not model program demand, licensing, accreditation, or student pipeline.
